literal: With him who leaves my sulking to wither, my heart saying 'we will unite' is a futile desire.
translation: For my heart to think, 'We will unite with him,' who simply leaves my sulking to wither away without consoling me, is a futile, helpless longing.
modern: ஊடலைத் தணிக்காமல் அது தானாகவே வாடிப் போகும்படி விட்டுவிடுகின்ற காதலரோடு, 'நாம் கூடுவோம்' என்று என் நெஞ்சம் நினைப்பது வீணான ஆசையாகும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the helpless nature of her own heart. When she enters a love-quarrel (ūṭal), her lover does not try to comfort her, but instead leaves her until her anger withers (uṇaṅka) away on its own. Despite this neglect, her heart still eagerly longs to reunite with him. She describes this persistent urge of her heart to seek union as a futile, uncontrollable desire (avā).
